title: ReMARk: A multi-level strategy to address disparities in rural HPV-related cancer prevention
text:
The proposed research is relevant to public health because it has significant promise to identify localized
areas for tailoring or targeting cancer prevention efforts, and therefore, reduce cancer rates, especially in rural
areas. The project increases the impact of the ReMARk study by conducting spatial analysis with fine-scale
geographically linked medical datasets to understand the broader context in which current cancer prevention
and control interventions are being implemented. The proposed research is relevant to NIH’s mission to
prevent cancer for all persons within the United States.

title: Investigating the role of TLR5 signaling as a modulator of FLT3 ligand therapeutic efficacy for the treatment of ovarian cancer
text:
Immune therapy for ovarian cancer has largely been ineffective, and the mechanistic basis for this failure remains
unknown. This study will provide novel insight into the role that chronic TLR5 signaling shapes the ovarian tumor
microenvironment, and how these microenvironmental changes impact the function and efficacy of dendritic-cell
expanding therapy using FLT3L. This research proposal has the potential to define targetable pathways to
mitigate the negative effects of TLR5 signaling on dendritic cells within the ovarian tumor microenvironment,
enhancing the efficacy of immune therapy for patients with ovarian cancer.

title: Top-down modulation of the dorsal cochlear nucleus
text:
Top-down contextual information modulates the processing of bottom-up auditory signals to improve
hearing accuracy, but the neural mechanisms underlying this essential function remain unclear, especially at
the earliest level of the central auditory system. Here we use modern in vitro and in vivo approaches in mice to
examine the role of the massive top-down projection from the inferior colliculus to the dorsal cochlear nucleus
and test the cellular and circuit mechanism that guide context-dependent filtering of bottom-up signals. This
project may provide insight into ways to improve auditory perception when bottom-up signals are degraded due
to hearing loss, as well as auditory processing disorders for which dysfunctional top-down modulation has
been implicated.

title: Genital Immune, Mucosal, and Viral Effects of Female Genital Schistosomiasis in Tanzania
text:
The proposed research is relevant to public health because it addresses the unmet need for adequate
treatment strategies for female genital schistosomiasis (FGS), which causes persistent genital mucosal
disease in approximately 70% of women despite treatment with anti-schistosome praziquantel therapy. By
identifying genital mucosal immune, epithelial, and viral alterations that persist after praziquantel therapy, we
may identify novel therapeutic strategies that could include modifying the host mucosal immune response,
promoting epithelial healing, and suppressing mucosal viral shedding. Therefore, this proposed research is
relevant to the NIH's mission of fostering “innovative research strategies… for protecting and improving
health,” as well as specifically responsive to the NIAID's goal to better understand and treat one of “the world's
most intractable and wide-spread diseases,” with potential to improve the lives of millions of girls and women
suffering from chronic FGS in Africa.

title: The role of NFIB-MAST1 signaling in mediating adaptive cisplatin resistance in SCLC
text:
Treatment with platinum-based drugs in small cell lung cancer (SCLC) often results in the development of
resistance leading to therapeutic failure, but the mechanisms remain unclear. We found that cisplatin activates
NFIB-MAST1-PLK1 signals to confer adaptive resistance in ASCL1-high SCLC. In this proposal, we will continue
to delineate the complex network governed by NFIB-MAST1 that confers cisplatin resistance in SCLC.

title: Dana Farber/Harvard Cancer Center SPORE in Lung Cancer
text:
This is a resubmission application for a SPORE in Lung Cancer from the Lung Cancer Program of the Dana-
Farber/Harvard Cancer Center (DF/HCC). The DF/HCC seeks to capitalize on important gains in targeted and
immunotherapy of lung cancer and develop innovative translational strategies designed to improve lung cancer
cure rates.

title: Developing ER Stress Chemical Modulators as Neuroprotectants for Glaucoma
text:
Neuroprotectant is urgently needed for glaucoma treatment. The proposed experiments are built on solid
previous results and promising preliminary data to advance lead compounds into optimized preclinical drug
candidates. In vivo efficacies of these novel treatments will be further determined at both bulk and single-cell
levels using our newly developed techniques in inducible and reversible ocular hypertension glaucoma mouse
models.

title: Structural definition of CD4-induced HIV-1 Env conformational changes required for infection
text:
In this grant we will investigate the stepwise conformational changes of the HIV-1 envelope (Env) protein
during receptor mediated entry into host cells. The focus of Aim 1 will be on the early stages of Env opening,
including the role that the unique FP configuration in HIV-1 plays in the metastability of the pre-fusion, pre-
receptor, closed Env and how this impacts the Env conformational landscape, of Aim 2 will be on detailed
characterization of a newly defined intermediate state where the HIV-1 fusion peptide (FP) retains ability to
bind broadly neutralizing antibodies (bnAbs) despite substantial Env opening, and of Aim 3 will be on later
stages of Env opening where the FP gets buried within a hydrophibic core and is no longer available for
antibody binding. These studies will advance our understanding of the HIV-1 entry mechanism and inform
structure-based immunogen and drug design.

title: Examining The Role of Corticothalamic Loops in the Prefrontal Cortex in Temporal Lobe Epilepsy
text:
One third of individuals living with epilepsy do not respond to current therapies, underscoring the need to
identify novel targets to treat seizures; network-based therapies are a promising direction but require identifying
new circuit-based targets. Despite widespread connectivity with other components of seizure generating
networks, the role of thalamic-to-prefrontal cortex circuits in development and control of seizures have not been
comprehensively studied. Targeting prefrontal cortex offers a novel target for understanding epilepsy-associated
changes in brain circuitry, and a novel target for controlling seizures to improve outcomes for people living with
epilepsy.

title: CRISOL Mente: A Multilevel Community Intervention to Reduce Mental Health Disparities Among Latinos
text:
Latinos in the U.S. experience significant barriers to access mental health services due to lack of health
insurance, language barriers, low availability of bilingual providers, and negative attitudes towards individuals
affected by mental health. There is an urgent need to identify low-cost and appropriate interventions to meet
the mental health needs of this population. This project will address that need by implementing and testing
CRISOL Mente, a multi-level, community-engaged intervention to improve access to mental health services
among the Latino population in Philadelphia.

title: The role of AgRP neurons in the metabolic and reproductive complications of Cushing's Syndrome
text:
Cushing’s syndrome is caused by exogenous or endogenous glucocorticoid excess which results in several
complications, including metabolic syndrome and infertility, yet the mechanism leading to these tightly linked
complications is not well understood. The objective of this proposal is to decipher the role of Agouti-Related
Protein (AgRP) neurons, known orexigenic neurons, in mediating the glucocorticoid-induced metabolic and
reproductive effects. The goal of this career development award is to investigate the neuroendocrine
mechanisms underlying the dysregulation of reproductive and metabolic functions under chronic corticosteroid
excess and its epigenetic consequences, through a series of genetic mouse and viral models and
pharmacological approaches, to develop novel therapeutic approaches to improve metabolic and reproductive
complications of patients with Cushing’s syndrome.

title: CRISPR-TB for pediatric TB diagnosis and treatment response
text:
Children under 5 years of age account for ~50% of the 1.2 million new cases of pediatric TB each year, but are
least likely to be diagnosed as they often present with disseminated or extrapulmonary TB and paucibacillary
disease, and are therefore often missed by respiratory sampling, and are at highest risk of death without prompt
treatment.
To meet the need of non-sputum diagnostic tools for TB in young children, we developed an assay that detects
Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb) cell free DNA (cfDNA) coupled with CRISPR technology (CRISPR-TB) to
improve sensitivity using small blood volumes.
The proposed study will utilize samples from an ongoing large well-characterized cohort of children with
suspected TB as well as additional cohorts of adults with confirmed TB and their asymptomatic household
controls, and recently BCG-immunized asymptomatic infants to evaluate CRISPR-TB diagnostic performance
(Aim 1) including longitudinal evaluation for treatment response (Aim 2), and extend evaluation to urine samples
(Aim 3).

title: Duke Research Training Program in Surgical Oncology
text: There is a critical need for surgeons knowledgeable in the clinical aspects of oncology and skilled in modern scientific methods that will provide novel approaches to the understanding and treatment of cancer. Development of highly skilled surgeon scientists requires dedicated time for research training and mentorship experience, which will be provided to residents and fellows who participate in the proposed training program.

title: Next generation of AAV vector targeting adipose tissue
text:
Adeno-associated viral (AAV) vectors are mainstream delivery platforms in gene therapy, yet AAV-
mediated gene transfer to adipose tissue is left far behind due to the low transduction efficiency and tropism of
natural AAV serotypes. Our preliminary studies have found a newly engineered capsid LC.V7 to possess
exclusive adipose-tropism while eliminating transduction of liver and other peripheral tissues. This project aims
to develop the next generation of AAV vector platform for adipose gene delivery based on the novel LC.V7 capsid,
which will provide a powerful tool for basic research and therapeutic purposes.

title: The Impacts of Adverse Provider Conditions on Medical Decision-Making and Patient Care.
text: The primary goal of the present proposal is to use a rigorous multi-method approach to determine how and when adverse provider conditions (e.g., burnout, illness, concerns about own health, and inflammation) lead to lower quality of care, especially for patients from certain groups. The proposed research points to potential and novel factors that negatively affect clinical decision-making that have time-dependent opportunities for intervention, distinct from (but complementary to) current approaches. Moreover, the proposed research will provide additional, novel evidence supporting the importance of addressing system-level issues of inadequate staffing and provider burnout.

title: Understanding Phosphatidylserine (PS) as a Signaling Moiety during Differentiation
text:
Phosphatidylserine (PS) is a phospholipid that cells actively keep on the inner leaflet of the plasma membrane,
with controlled exposure of PS on the outer leaflet acting as a signal for intercellular communication. While PS
exposure is well known in apoptosis, this proposal examines the role of PS in cellular differentiation, during
adipogenesis. Our investigations into mechanisms of PS exposure and its relevance adipose tissue
accumulation is expected to have direct impact for fat tissue inflammation and obesity.

title: Novel deep learning frameworks for predicting nucleosome-binding proteins
text:
Novel deep learning frameworks for predicting nucleosome-binding proteins
Nucleosome-binding proteins play an important role in development and organogenesis, but the experimental
techniques used to identify them are insensitive, expensive or time consuming. This proposal aims to develop a
novel two-stage transfer learning framework to predict these proteins by combining sequence and structural
information. It will also implement a new transfer learning-continual learning framework that not only predicts the
nucleosome binders in a species-specific manner, but also accommodates progressively available nucleosome-
protein interaction data without forgetting previously learned knowledge.

title: Mechanisms of Dysglycemia in People with Cirrhosis and Liver Transplant Recipients
text:
The proposal is relevant to public health because it provides several approaches to improving diagnosis of
dysglycemia, which is prominent in many chronic diseases, including liver disease. It focuses on determining
how measurements that can easily be obtained in clinic can act as surrogates for underlying mechanisms of
dysglycemia. It is relevant to the NIH’s missions as its accomplishment will allow for better prediction of
outcomes, personalized treatment, and development of better therapies for this vulnerable population while
providing cross-disciplinary research training to a new investigator working at the intersection of machine
learning, diabetes, and liver disease.

title: Molecular Imaging Guidance for Potentiating Chemoimmunotherapy in Pancreatic Cancer using Photodynamic Priming
text:
Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma is the 3rd deadliest cancer in the US with only 3% of patients surviving beyond
5 years after the cancer has spread. Less than 25% of patients are eligible for surgery, and the effects of
chemotherapy and immunotherapy are limited by various barriers in the tumor immediate environment. This
project harnesses a light-activated priming treatment to restore the effects of chemotherapy, improve the immune
system’s ability to eliminate the tumor, and prolong survival rates.

title: Hypoxia-associated L-2-hydroxyglutarate in regulation of germinal center responses
text:
B cells aid in immune responses to pathogens by undergoing activation in the germinal center and
differentiating either into plasma cells, which produce antibodies, or memory B cells, which can quickly respond
to the same pathogen upon re-exposure. B cells in the germinal center experience low levels of oxygen, which
has previously been shown to affect B cell function and fate, but the signals that govern this process are not
well understood. My proposal will study how germinal center B cells are regulated by L-2-hydroxyglutarate,
which is produced in cells under low oxygen conditions and an inhibitor of enzymes that regulate DNA
accessibility, expanding our knowledge of how B cells choose their fate.
